about: StoryStudio shot types, from the Shot type library. To add your own or change one, put my_shottypes.json in StoryStudio's own folder (next to settings.json): a list of types, or {"types": [...]}; a type with the same code replaces the built-in one, a new code is added. That file can also hold its own "mix" (and "scene_unit"), which is used instead of the one here. cameras must be MiniMax camera commands. characters is [fewest, most] recurring characters on screen. extra: true = usually an extra shot, false = usually a main shot, null = either.

types.name: Establishing wide
types.purpose: Tells the viewer where they are; opens a scene or resets after a change of place
types.framing: The place dominates; any character is small in the distance or absent
types.guidance: Describe exactly what is in the place, so the image AI doesn't add buildings or people of its own

types.name: Wide / full figure
types.purpose: Shows the whole body and what it is doing; physical action lives here
types.framing: Character head to foot, with the place readable around them
types.guidance: Legs and walking go wrong most often here; keep the action simple and slow

types.name: Medium
types.purpose: The workhorse connector: body language plus some face
types.framing: Waist or chest up (for an animal, shoulders forward)
types.guidance: The safest shot to make, but a connector, not the default: don't let it crowd out close-ups and reactions

types.name: Close-up
types.purpose: The emotional beat; in a film without dialogue this is the dialogue
types.framing: Head and a little shoulder, eyes on the upper third, background soft
types.guidance: One face, one feeling, with small movement; the clip is trimmed to its best seconds in the edit, so a close-up suits any clip length

types.name: Extreme close-up
types.purpose: The peak moment: one emotion, nowhere to hide
types.framing: The face fills the frame, or just the eyes
types.guidance: Save it for the real turning points, three or four in a whole film at most

types.name: Two-shot
types.purpose: The relationship: who is close to whom, and who is turned away
types.framing: Both characters in frame, usually one nearer the camera, not overlapping
types.guidance: The hardest type to make: keep the two apart, give only one of them something to do while the other holds still, and frame tighter (heads and shoulders) when you can

types.name: Over the shoulder
types.purpose: Puts the viewer on one character's side of the scene
types.framing: A soft shoulder or back of a head in the near corner, the other character sharp beyond
types.guidance: Describe the near character loosely, just a shape and a colour; detail there gets redrawn wrong

types.name: Point of view
types.purpose: Makes the viewer the character for a moment
types.framing: What the character is looking at, from their eye height; the watcher is not on screen
types.guidance: Cheap and reliable because no character has to stay the same; list no characters for it

types.name: Insert / detail
types.purpose: Points at the one object the story turns on
types.framing: Tight on a thing, not a face
types.guidance: Almost always works; use it instead of showing a hand picking up or carrying something, since hands gripping objects often come out wrong: show the object already moving or already in place

types.name: Reaction
types.purpose: Tells the audience how to feel about what just happened
types.framing: Close-up or medium on whoever is watching
types.guidance: The most underused type: when a beat feels flat, a reaction shot after it is usually what's missing

types.name: Tracking / following
types.purpose: Movement with momentum: travelling, chasing, walking away
types.framing: The character moving, the camera moving with them
types.guidance: Costly to get right: keep the movement slow, or frame it tight so less of the body shows

types.name: Foreground wipe
types.purpose: A transition disguised as a shot: something crosses close to the lens and the cut happens inside it
types.framing: Any view, with a branch, a shape or a passer-by sweeping close across the front
types.guidance: Generic and reusable: describe the view and the thing passing close in front of the camera

types.name: Empty frame
types.purpose: Aftermath, loneliness, time passing: the character has gone, or hasn't arrived
types.framing: The place with nobody in it
types.guidance: The strongest shot for sadness and the cheapest to make: describe the place as still and deserted, and put one after a loss
